## What this page shows

The weak-lensing likelihood of a galaxy needs the probability of its observed ellipticity
$\epsilon_{\rm obs}$ at the shear $g$, marginalized over the intrinsic ellipticity
$\chi_I$:
$$
P(\epsilon_{\rm obs} \mid g) = \int_{|\chi_I| < 1} P_{\rm 2D}(\chi_I)\, N_2\!\left(\epsilon_{\rm obs} - f_g(\chi_I)\right) \mathrm{d}^2\chi_I,
$$
where $P_{\rm 2D}$ is the intrinsic-ellipticity population, $N_2$ the isotropic Gaussian
of per-component dispersion $\sigma_{\rm noise}$ (`std_noise`), and $f_g$ the shear map of
the ellipticity convention (TRACE or TRACE_DET). The
[framework page](../theory/nc/lss/galaxy/galaxy_wl_framework.qmd) defines both conventions.

NumCosmo has four classes that compute or approximate this integral:

- `NcGalaxyShapeFactorVarAdd`: the observed ellipticity pulled back through the inverse
  shear map and evaluated on a Gaussian of variance $\sigma^2 + \sigma_{\rm noise}^2$; it
  needs the dispersion $\sigma$ of a Gaussian population;
- `NcGalaxyShapeFactorMomentsGauss`: a Gaussian with the exact mean and variances of the
  sheared, noisy marginal;
- `NcGalaxyShapeFactorMomentsTilt`: the exact zero-shear marginal with an exponential tilt
  fixed by the same exact moments, interpolated in $\min(|g|, 1/|g|)$ from tables built
  per population and noise;
- `NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral`: the integral by adaptive Chebyshev panels in polar
  coordinates ([theory page](../theory/nc/lss/galaxy/wl_shape_marginalization_spectral.qmd)).

The reference is the release asset `nc_galaxy_shape_marginal_arb_cert.bin`, written by
`tests/tools/make_shape_marginal_arb_table.py` from values certified by the Arb tool
`tests/tools/nc_galaxy_shape_marginal_arb.c`. Each of its 26,023 points has a certified
$\ln P$ rounded to the nearest double. The points cover both conventions; the truncated
Gaussian with $\sigma \in \{0.05, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4\}$ and seven Beta populations in
$r = |\chi_I|$; $\sigma_{\rm noise}$ from 0.005 to 1; $|g|$ from 0 to 3; and
$|\epsilon_{\rm obs}|$ from 0 to 2. This page reads the table and evaluates every class at
every point it supports, with the default settings of each class.

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
import time

import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

from numcosmo_py import Nc, Ncm

Ncm.cfg_init()

plt.rcParams.update(
    {
        "figure.dpi": 110,
        "font.size": 12,
        "axes.titlesize": 12,
        "axes.labelsize": 12,
        "xtick.labelsize": 10,
        "ytick.labelsize": 10,
    }
)

COLS = ["conv", "pop", "p1", "p2", "std_noise", "g1", "g2", "e1", "e2", "lnP"]
C = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(COLS)}
CONV = {0: Nc.GalaxyWLObsEllipConv.TRACE, 1: Nc.GalaxyWLObsEllipConv.TRACE_DET}
CONV_NAME = {0: "TRACE", 1: "TRACE_DET"}
POP_NAME = {0: "Gauss", 1: "Beta"}
CLASSES = {
    "VarAdd": (Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorVarAdd, False),
    "MomentsGauss": (Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorMomentsGauss, True),
    "MomentsTilt": (Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorMomentsTilt, True),
    "Spectral": (Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorSpectral, True),
}
FAIL = 0.5  # |Delta ln P| above which a point is marked as failing

ser = Ncm.Serialize.new(Ncm.SerializeOpt.NONE)
table = ser.dict_str_from_binfile(
    Nc.data_download_release_file("nc_galaxy_shape_marginal_arb_cert.bin")
).get("points")
points = np.array(table.dup_array()).reshape(table.nrows(), table.ncols())


def build_mset(pop):
    """The models a NcGalaxyShapeFactorData needs; only pop enters ln P here."""
    cosmo = Nc.HICosmoDEXcdm.new()
    dist = Nc.Distance.new(100.0)
    hms = Nc.HaloCMParam.new(Nc.HaloMassSummaryMassDef.MEAN, 200.0)
    hp = Nc.HaloPosition.new(dist)
    hp.param_set_by_name("z", 0.2)
    hp.prepare(cosmo)
    mset = Ncm.MSet.empty_new()
    for model in (
        cosmo,
        Nc.HaloDensityProfileNFW.new(hms),
        hp,
        Nc.WLSurfaceMassDensity.new(dist),
        pop,
        Nc.GalaxyRedshiftPopLSSTSRD.new_y1_source(),
        Nc.GalaxyRedshiftObsGauss.new(),
    ):
        mset.set(model)
    return mset


def new_pop(ip, p1, p2):
    """The truncated Gaussian (ip = 0, sigma = p1) or the Beta population (ip = 1)."""
    if ip == 0:
        pop = Nc.GalaxyShapePopGauss.new()
        pop["sigma"] = p1
    else:
        pop = Nc.GalaxyShapePopBeta.new()
        pop["alpha"] = p1
        pop["beta"] = p2
    return pop


def evaluate(cls):
    """ln P of cls at every point (NaN where unsupported) and the time per point.

    One data object per convention, population and noise; the first evaluation of each
    includes what the class builds for them (the MomentsTilt tables).
    """
    lnp = np.full(len(points), np.nan)
    sec = np.full(len(points), np.nan)
    keys = np.unique(points[:, 0:5], axis=0)
    for conv, ip, p1, p2, sn in keys:
        if ip == 1 and not CLASSES[cls][1]:
            continue
        idx = np.flatnonzero(np.all(points[:, 0:5] == (conv, ip, p1, p2, sn), axis=1))
        pop = new_pop(ip, p1, p2)
        mset = build_mset(pop)
        gsf = CLASSES[cls][0].new(CONV[int(conv)])
        pos_data = Nc.GalaxyPositionFactorData.new(
            Nc.GalaxyPositionFactorFlat.new(-1.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1.0), mset
        )
        z_data = Nc.GalaxyRedshiftFactorData.new(
            Nc.GalaxyRedshiftFactorComposed.new(0.0, 20.0), mset
        )
        data = Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorData.new(gsf, mset, pos_data, z_data)
        gsf.data_set(
            data, 0.0, 0.0, sn, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, Nc.WLEllipticityFrame.CELESTIAL
        )
        gsf.prepare_data_array(mset, [data], True, True)
        for i in idx:
            g1, g2, e1, e2 = points[i, C["g1"] : C["e2"] + 1]
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            lnp[i] = gsf.eval_ln_marginal(pop, data, g1, g2, e1, e2)
            sec[i] = time.perf_counter() - t0
    return lnp, sec


results = {cls: evaluate(cls) for cls in CLASSES}
abs_g = np.round(np.hypot(points[:, C["g1"]], points[:, C["g2"]]), 6)
abs_e = np.round(np.hypot(points[:, C["e1"]], points[:, C["e2"]]), 6)
```

## Accuracy

The error of a class at a point is
$$
\Delta \ln P \equiv \ln P - \ln P_0,
$$
where $\ln P_0$ is the certified value. Where $|\Delta \ln P| \ll 1$ it is the relative
error of $P$, since $\Delta P / P_0 = e^{\Delta \ln P} - 1$. A point fails when
$|\Delta \ln P| > 0.5$, a factor $e^{0.5} \approx 1.65$ in $P$, or when the class returns a
value that is not finite.

Below that threshold no value is marked as acceptable. The likelihood of a catalog of $N$
galaxies is a sum over galaxies, so an error of the same sign in every galaxy changes
$-2 \ln L$ by up to $2N |\Delta \ln P|$. Its effect on the cluster parameters depends on how
the error varies with $g$ across the catalog, and it is known only after it is propagated
to the parameters.

Each figure shows one class at the shears $|g| \le 0.3$. No galaxy of the curated HSC
catalogs reaches $|g| = 0.3$ for an NFW halo of mass up to $10^{15.3}\,M_\odot$ at the
catalog's own cluster position, redshift and concentration. A cell is one pair
($\sigma_{\rm noise}$, $|\epsilon_{\rm obs}|$). Its color is the median $|\Delta \ln P|$ over
the populations of the family, the shears and the directions in the cell, and its label is
the percentage of failing points. A cell without a label has no failing point. The table
below each figure gives the same counts for $|g| \le 0.3$ and for $|g| > 0.3$.

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
SN = np.unique(points[:, C["std_noise"]])
ES = np.unique(abs_e)
G_MAX = 0.3
VMIN, VMAX = -14.0, 2.0


def cell_grid(cls, conv, ip):
    """log10 of the median |Delta ln P| and the failing fraction per cell."""
    d = np.abs(results[cls][0] - points[:, C["lnP"]])
    d[~np.isfinite(d)] = np.inf
    evaluated = CLASSES[cls][1] or ip == 0
    median = np.full((len(SN), len(ES)), np.nan)
    failing = np.full((len(SN), len(ES)), np.nan)
    if not evaluated:
        return median, failing
    sel0 = (
        (points[:, C["conv"]] == conv) & (points[:, C["pop"]] == ip) & (abs_g <= G_MAX)
    )
    for a, sn in enumerate(SN):
        for b, e in enumerate(ES):
            sel = sel0 & (points[:, C["std_noise"]] == sn) & (abs_e == e)
            if np.any(sel):
                median[a, b] = np.log10(max(np.median(d[sel]), 1.0e-16))
                failing[a, b] = np.mean(d[sel] > FAIL)
    return median, failing


def plot_class(cls):
    """Four panels: TRACE and TRACE_DET by Gauss and Beta."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(9.0, 6.4), sharex=True, sharey=True)
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("viridis").copy()
    cmap.set_bad("0.85")
    for row, conv in enumerate((0, 1)):
        for col, ip in enumerate((0, 1)):
            ax = axes[row, col]
            median, failing = cell_grid(cls, conv, ip)
            im = ax.imshow(
                median, origin="lower", cmap=cmap, vmin=VMIN, vmax=VMAX, aspect="auto"
            )
            for a, b in zip(*np.nonzero(failing > 0.0)):
                ax.text(
                    b, a, f"{100.0 * failing[a, b]:.0f}", ha="center", va="center",
                    color="red", fontsize=9,
                )
            if np.all(np.isnan(median)):
                ax.text(
                    0.5 * (len(ES) - 1), 0.5 * (len(SN) - 1), "not supported",
                    ha="center", va="center",
                )
            ax.set_title(f"{CONV_NAME[conv]}, {POP_NAME[ip]}")
            ax.set_xticks(range(len(ES)), [f"{e:g}" for e in ES], rotation=45)
            ax.set_yticks(range(len(SN)), [f"{s:g}" for s in SN])
    for ax in axes[1, :]:
        ax.set_xlabel(r"$|\epsilon_{\rm obs}|$")
    for ax in axes[:, 0]:
        ax.set_ylabel(r"$\sigma_{\rm noise}$")
    fig.colorbar(
        im, ax=axes,
        label=r"$\log_{10}$ median $|\Delta \ln P|$, $|g| \leq 0.3$",
    )
    plt.show()


def failure_summary(cls):
    """Points, failing points and median |Delta ln P| per family and shear range."""
    d = np.abs(results[cls][0] - points[:, C["lnP"]])
    d[~np.isfinite(d)] = np.inf
    lines = [
        "| convention | population | shears | points | failing | median $|\\Delta \\ln P|$ |",
        "|---|---|---|---|---|---|",
    ]
    for conv in (0, 1):
        for ip in (0, 1):
            if not (CLASSES[cls][1] or ip == 0):
                lines.append(
                    f"| {CONV_NAME[conv]} | {POP_NAME[ip]} | all | not supported | | |"
                )
                continue
            fam = (points[:, C["conv"]] == conv) & (points[:, C["pop"]] == ip)
            for label, rng in (
                (r"$|g| \le 0.3$", abs_g <= G_MAX),
                (r"$|g| > 0.3$", abs_g > G_MAX),
            ):
                sel = fam & rng
                bad = d[sel] > FAIL
                lines.append(
                    f"| {CONV_NAME[conv]} | {POP_NAME[ip]} | {label} | {sel.sum():,} | "
                    f"{bad.sum():,} ({100.0 * bad.mean():.0f}%) | {np.median(d[sel]):.1e} |"
                )
    display(Markdown("\n".join(lines)))
```

## Speed

The approximate classes evaluate $\ln P$ in closed form or from tables. Spectral integrates,
which costs about two orders of magnitude more per evaluation. When the population is fixed,
Spectral can instead build, once per galaxy, an interpolant of $\ln P$ in $g$ on
$|g| \le 0.3$ (`NcGalaxyShapeFactorSpectral:use-interp`), and every later evaluation reads
the interpolant. When the population varies, as in a fit of its parameters, the interpolant
of every galaxy changes at every step, so each evaluation integrates.

The first table gives the median time per evaluation of each class over the certified points
above. The second gives, for 30 points of the fitted Beta population (TRACE,
$\alpha = 1.92$, $\beta = 1.98$) with $|\epsilon_{\rm obs}| < 1$ and
$\sigma_{\rm noise} \in \{0.03, 0.1, 0.3\}$, the time to build the interpolant, the time per
evaluation from it and by integration, at 200 and 20 random shears with $|g| \le 0.3$, and the
number of evaluations per galaxy above which building the interpolant costs less than
integrating. All times are measured on the machine that renders this page, on one thread,
through the Python bindings: a call through them costs of the order of half a microsecond,
which is most of the time of the approximate classes and of the interpolant (an evaluation of
the interpolant from C takes of the order of 0.1 µs).

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
lines = ["| class | median time per evaluation |", "|---|---|"]
for cls in CLASSES:
    sec = results[cls][1]
    lines.append(f"| {cls} | {np.nanmedian(sec) * 1.0e6:.1f} µs |")
display(Markdown("\n".join(lines)))
```

```{python}
# | code-fold: true
SPEED_SN = (0.03, 0.1, 0.3)
rng = np.random.default_rng(20261113)
speed_sel = (
    (points[:, C["conv"]] == 0)
    & (points[:, C["pop"]] == 1)
    & (points[:, C["p1"]] == 1.92)
    & np.isin(points[:, C["std_noise"]], SPEED_SN)
    & (abs_e < 1.0)
)
speed_gal = np.unique(points[speed_sel][:, [C["std_noise"], C["e1"], C["e2"]]], axis=0)
speed_gal = speed_gal[rng.choice(len(speed_gal), size=30, replace=False)]


def random_shears(n):
    """n shears uniform in the disc |g| <= 0.3."""
    r = 0.3 * np.sqrt(rng.uniform(size=n))
    t = rng.uniform(0.0, 2.0 * np.pi, size=n)
    return r * np.cos(t), r * np.sin(t)


def time_galaxy(sn, e1, e2):
    """Build time, time per interpolant evaluation and per integral, in seconds."""
    pop = new_pop(1, 1.92, 1.98)
    mset = build_mset(pop)
    gsf = Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorSpectral.new(Nc.GalaxyWLObsEllipConv.TRACE)
    gsf.set_use_interp(True)
    pos_data = Nc.GalaxyPositionFactorData.new(
        Nc.GalaxyPositionFactorFlat.new(-1.0, 1.0, -1.0, 1.0), mset
    )
    z_data = Nc.GalaxyRedshiftFactorData.new(
        Nc.GalaxyRedshiftFactorComposed.new(0.0, 20.0), mset
    )
    data = Nc.GalaxyShapeFactorData.new(gsf, mset, pos_data, z_data)
    gsf.data_set(data, e1, e2, sn, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, Nc.WLEllipticityFrame.CELESTIAL)
    gsf.prepare_data_array(mset, [data], True, True)

    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    gsf.data_prepare(mset, data, 3.0)
    t_build = time.perf_counter() - t0

    g1, g2 = random_shears(200)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for a, b in zip(g1, g2):
        gsf.eval_ln_marginal(pop, data, a, b, e1, e2)
    t_interp = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(g1)

    gsf.set_use_interp(False)
    g1, g2 = random_shears(20)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    for a, b in zip(g1, g2):
        gsf.eval_ln_marginal(pop, data, a, b, e1, e2)
    t_direct = (time.perf_counter() - t0) / len(g1)
    return t_build, t_interp, t_direct


speed = np.array([time_galaxy(*row) for row in speed_gal])
break_even = speed[:, 0] / (speed[:, 2] - speed[:, 1])


def quantiles(v, scale, fmt):
    """Median, 90% and largest of v times scale."""
    q = np.quantile(v, [0.5, 0.9, 1.0]) * scale
    return " / ".join(fmt.format(x) for x in q)


display(
    Markdown(
        "\n".join(
            [
                "| quantity (30 points) | median / 90% / largest |",
                "|---|---|",
                f"| build of the interpolant | {quantiles(speed[:, 0], 1.0, '{:.2f} s')} |",
                f"| evaluation from the interpolant | {quantiles(speed[:, 1], 1.0e6, '{:.1f} µs')} |",
                f"| evaluation by integration | {quantiles(speed[:, 2], 1.0e6, '{:.0f} µs')} |",
                f"| evaluations per galaxy where the build pays | {quantiles(break_even, 1.0, '{:.0f}')} |",
            ]
        )
    )
)
```

An MCMC of a cluster evaluates each galaxy at every step of every walker, of the order of
$10^5$ times, far above the break-even count: with a fixed population the build pays even if
it is repeated in every process of the run. The command `numcosmo wl-catalog shape-interp`
does it once instead. It builds the interpolants of all the galaxies of a catalog in parallel
and writes them with the catalog; `numcosmo generate cluster-wl-load --data-file` then builds
an experiment that loads them. The table below gives the measurements on the HSC field
HWL16a-094 (2,200 galaxies, fitted Beta population, TRACE).

| HWL16a-094, 2,200 galaxies | time |
|---|---|
| `wl-catalog shape-interp`, 12 threads | 44 s |
| the same build on 1 thread (`nc_data_cluster_wl_factor_data_prepare()`) | 450 s |
| first $-2\ln L$ of an experiment from the prepared catalog | 0.02 s |
| first $-2\ln L$ of the same experiment from the original catalog (builds every interpolant) | 447 s |
| MCMC, 1,000 walkers and 150,000 points, 12 threads, each thread building its interpolants | 736 s |
| the same MCMC from the prepared catalog | 221 s |

Measured on an AMD Ryzen 9 9900X (12 cores) on 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13, with fixed-node
redshift integration. The two experiments give the same $-2\ln L$ to the last digit, and the
two MCMCs the same posterior within the Monte Carlo error ($\log_{10} M_{200c}$ =
$15.4785 \pm 0.1211$ and $15.4785 \pm 0.1208$).
